pages.transcription:
Foreword
This book gathers what the Alderwick family remembered
in the autumn of 1992, set down by Edith Alderwick
from letters, kitchen-table talk and one tin box
of photographs. It is not a finished history.
Where memory and paper disagree we have said so.
pages.interpretation_note: The foreword speaks of 'one tin box'; no other page mentions it, so its contents are unknown.

pages.alt: Chapter One opening page, typeset, with a drop heading and nine lines of text.
pages.transcription:
CHAPTER ONE
The Mill at Marrowby

Tobias Alderwick was born in the spring of 1861
in the cottage beside Marrowby mill, the third
of seven children. His father kept the sluice
and his mother kept the accounts, such as they were.

He is said to have walked to Harlowe fair at nine
and come home with a goose and a sixpence.
pages.interpretation_note: 'Said to have walked' signals family hearsay, not a recorded fact.

pages.alt: Typeset page, scanned upside down and rotated to read correctly; slight skew visible.
pages.transcription:
In 1889 Tobias married Hester Pell at St Oswin's,
Marrowby. The register, we are told, was
signed with a steady hand on both sides.

Their first child, Walter, arrived the next winter.
The cottage was by then too small, so the
family moved up the lane to Sluice House.
pages.interpretation_note: Reader suspects 'steady hand' may be a later gloss; the scan is faint at line 3.

pages.alt: Mounted sepia photograph of a stern couple before a stone house; below it a handwritten pencil caption.
pages.transcription: Tobias & Hester, outside Sluice House, c. 1895
pages.interpretation_note: Date 'c. 1895' is the captioner's guess, written in a different hand from the name.

pages.alt: Hand-ruled family diagram: Tobias Alderwick married to Hester Pell, with a line down to their son Walter.
pages.transcription:
Tobias Alderwick (b. 1861) = Hester Pell (b. 1865)
Walter Alderwick (b. 1890)
pages.interpretation_note: The diagram gives Tobias's birth year as 1861, matching p004; ink has been darkened on 'Walter'.

pages.alt: Typeset page with six lines and a faint coffee ring in the lower corner.
pages.transcription:
Walter grew up at Sluice House and took over
the mill lease in 1912. He never spoke of
the years before, and we have not pressed him.

A cousin recalls a letter from overseas, kept
in the tin box, but nobody has seen it since.
pages.interpretation_note: The overseas letter is mentioned only here; no other source is cited.
